ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Extremely low white-to-black ratio; pixel intensity is dominated by low-value (dark) pixels across >98% of the visible surface, with high-intensity pixels confined to localized scar rings and barnacle clusters.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid dark-grey to black contiguous mapping across both lobes; high-contrast geometric blobs consist of approximately 18-22 circular white rings (5-15 pixel diameter) scattered across the mid-section of the left lobe and lower-central region of the right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 48 degrees; apex depth represents approximately 12% of the total vertical extent of the visible fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the entire trailing edge; pixel-amplitude of peaks and valleys varies between 4 and 22 pixels, creating a highly irregular and jagged linear boundary.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Moderate convexity on the trailing edge of both lobes, terminating in highly irregular, non-geometric jagged profiles at the lateral tips due to external biological attachments.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Distinct spatial clusters of circular high-contrast white rings (barnacle attachment scars) present on the medial and lateral regions of the left lobe and scattered on the proximal region of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Significant biological encrustations (sessile barnacle clusters) present on the distal tips of both lobes; the right tip exhibits a more extensive three-dimensional cluster that extends beyond the natural dermal boundary.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique irregular profile of the lateral tips caused by dense barnacle colonization, effectively masking the true geometric termination of the fluke structure.
